# Sections, presets, lists and repeats

Whole sections of a page, the saved presets a person inserts, the items of a component's list (slides, cards), and repeats that draw a part once per item of a collection, the pages or a menu.

## repeat.insert

Insert a repeat: a part drawn once for each item of its source (a collection's items, the site's pages, a menu), as child `index` of a parent. Use it to list a collection on a page: the template's parts read each item with `{ $item: '<field>' }` or `{ $bind: 'item.<field>' }`. To turn a part that exists into a repeat, tree.remove it and repeat.insert its nodes as the template at its place, in one batch. Refusals: `duplicate_id`, `orphan_node`, `invalid_node`, `invalid_input` (a template choice naming none of the template's roots); the validator's `collection.known` (no such collection), `repeat.caps`, `bind.context`.

## preset.set

Set or clear one of the site's presets whole: a saved part a person inserts copies of. Prefer preset.save, which saves a part as it stands on a page; send this to build a preset from nodes of your own, or `preset: null` to clear one. A preset holds the part's nodes from `part.root`, their translations, whether it is a section and the header or footer region it was the bar of. A page keeps the copy it inserted. Refused: `duplicate_key` (the key holds a preset of another kind, a starting motion), `orphan_node` and `invalid_input` (a node that does not hang from the root).

## preset.save

Save a part of a page or of a definition (a header's bar) as one of the site's presets, as it stands now. Part `node` of `at` is kept whole under `key` with its translations (`l10n: false` leaves them out); a later edit of the page does not change the preset, and a key already used is replaced. A section of its page becomes a section preset, the bar of a header or footer a bar that can take another bar's place, anything else a part that goes inside a section. Refused: `duplicate_key` (the key holds a preset of another kind), `op_target` (no such part, or the tree's root).

|---|---|---|---|

A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | The part to save: a node of the tree `at` names, not its root. |
| `l10n` | false |  | false: save the part without its translations. |

## preset.insert

Place a copy of one of the site's presets on a page or in a definition, under fresh ids: as child `index` of `parent`, or right before node `before`. The copy's root takes the preset's label as its name; `menus` names a node whose menus the copy shows, in order. To replace a header or footer bar, send preset.insert with `before` and `menus` both naming the old bar, then tree.remove of the bar, inside one component.edit of the region's definition. A whole section from a component is section.insert. Refused: `op_target` (no saved part under the key, a `before` with no parent, no such `menus` node), and what tree.insert refuses (`not_a_parent`, `duplicate_id`). Output: { root } of the copy.

- **op**; class `structure` (Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "section".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `key` | string | yes | The preset's key: lower-case words joined by -, up to 64 characters (the sections read lists the site's presets). |
| `parent` | string |  | The frame the copy goes in, with `index`. |
| `index` | integer ≥0 |  | The copy's place among the parent's children, from 0. |
| `before` | string |  | A node the copy goes right before, in that node's parent: instead of `parent` and `index`. |
| `menus` | string |  | A node whose menus the copy shows, in order: the bar it replaces. |

Example inputs:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"key":"citazione-cliente","parent":"x576co7y","index":2}
```


## section.insert

Add a section to a page: a new instance of a section component of the site, or a copy of a section of a page. It goes after section `after` or before section `before` (neither: at the end). From a component it shows its defaults and the values `source.props` gives; a copy from a page brings the motion wholly inside it (`motion: false`: none) and names motion it cannot bring in a `motion.left_behind` finding. A kind the site has not used yet is section.addKind, a saved part preset.insert. Refused: `section.not_a_section`, `section.component` (not a section component), `section.layout`, `unknown_component`, `section.no_holder`, `instance.required_prop` (a required prop left out). Output: { root } of the new section.

- **op**; class `sections` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "section".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | object | yes | The page: { page: <pageId> } (site_context lists the pages). |
| `at` › `page` | uuid | yes |  |
| `after` | string |  | The section of the page the new one goes right after. |
| `before` | string |  | The section of the page the new one goes right before; with neither, at the end. |
| `source` | { component: string, props?: Record<string, string \| number \| boolean \| null \| (… \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …)[] \| Record<string, … \| … \| … \| … \| … \| …>> } \| { page: uuid, node: string, name?: string (min 1, max 80) } | yes | What the new section is: a new instance of a section component, or a copy of a section of a page. |
| `motion` | false |  | false: the motion wholly inside the part stays where it is (none copied or taken); absent: it goes with the part. |
| `declares` | false |  | Leave it out: only a step stored before pages said which node holds their sections carries false. |


## section.move

Move a section of a page to another place among its sections, with everything it holds. It goes right after section `after` or right before section `before`; with neither, to the end of the page. Only whole sections move this way: a part inside a section moves with tree.move. Refused: `section.not_a_section` (`node`, `after` or `before` is not a section; for a part inside one, the refusal names that section), `invalid_input` (beside itself), `op_target` (no such node), `section.no_holder`.

## section.remove

Remove a section of a page with everything it holds, its translations and the motion wholly inside it, with the waits on that motion. `motion: false` leaves the motion, `waits: false` the waits. A part inside a section goes with tree.remove. Refused: `section.not_a_section`, `op_target` (no such node), `lock.removed` (a locked section: tree.set_locked unlocks it), `motion.starts_from_wait` (a timeline that stays starts from a wait it would take). Output: { took: { timelines, states, locks } } of the motion it took (`locks`: the gates that held the page's scroll), else null.

- **op**; class `sections` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "section".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | object | yes | The page: { page: <pageId> } (site_context lists the pages). |
| `at` › `page` | uuid | yes |  |
| `node` | string | yes | The section: one of the page's sections (a child of the node that holds them). |
| `motion` | false |  | false: the motion wholly inside the part stays where it is (none copied or taken); absent: it goes with the part. |
| `waits` | false |  | false: the waits on its motion stay (a gate that opens when one of its timelines ends). |
| `declares` | false |  | Leave it out: only a step stored before pages said which node holds their sections carries false. |


## section.holder

Say which node of a page holds its sections: its children are the page's sections, what the section ops move, copy and remove. `node` is a frame, group or vector of the page; no `node` takes the statement off, and the page is read by its shape. A new page states its root, and a section op states the holder on an older page that states none, so this is rarely needed. Refused: `unknown_page` (`at` is a definition), `op_target` (no such node).

## section.addKind

Add a section of one of the kinds every site can add to a page, though its design system has none: text-and-picture, questions-and-answers, contact-form, banner, gallery or cards. It goes right after section `after`, right before section `before`, else at the end. The first time, its definition `kind.<kind>` joins the design system in the site's tokens (a contact form also adds a form when the site has none); after that section.insert of `kind.<kind>` adds another. A list kind starts with a few items in the site's language. Refused: `section.not_a_section`, `section.no_holder`. Findings: `kind.colours`, a colour pair of the site the kind could not use. Output: { root } of the new section.

## slot.add

Add an item to a list of a component instance (a carousel's slides, a list's items, a grid's cards): slot `slot` of instance `node`, at `index` (absent: at the end). The item is a copy of one of the slot's items (`source.copy`, under fresh ids, with its translations, not its motion), or nodes of its own (`source.root` and `source.nodes`). Use it rather than instance.fillSlot, which replaces a slot's whole content. Refused: `slot.full` (the slot holds its most items), `slot.not_a_list`, `slot.unknown`, `slot.no_item` (the item to copy is not in the slot), `duplicate_id`, `orphan_node`, `invalid_input` (an index past the end). Output: { root } of the new item.

- **op**; class `sections` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "carousel", "slide", "card".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | The component instance that holds the list (node/<pageId>?node= reads its slots). |
| `slot` | string | yes | The list's slot name, as the instance's definition declares it (definition/<key> lists its slots). |
| `index` | integer ≥0 |  | Where the item goes among the slot's items, from 0; absent: at the end. |
| `source` | { copy: string, name?: string (min 1, max 80) } \| { root: string, nodes: Record<string, { name?: string (min 1, max 80), style?: Record<string, …>, attrs?: Record<string, …>, anchor?: string, hidden?: true, showOn?: "list" \| "item", audience?: { who: "members", … } \| { who: "guests", … }, locked?: true, meta?: Record<s… (the whole schema: discover_operations with names) | yes | A copy of one of the slot's items, or an item of nodes of its own. |

Example inputs:

```json

```

## slot.move

Move an item of a component instance's list to another place among the slot's items, with everything it holds. `index` is the place it takes, from 0, counted among the items. Refused: `slot.no_item` (not an item of the slot), `slot.not_a_list`, `slot.unknown`, `invalid_input` (an index past the last item).

- **op**; class `sections` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "carousel", "slide", "card", "reorder".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | The component instance that holds the list (node/<pageId>?node= reads its slots). |
| `slot` | string | yes | The list's slot name, as the instance's definition declares it (definition/<key> lists its slots). |
| `item` | string | yes | The item to move: one of the slot's items. |
| `index` | integer ≥0 | yes | The place it takes among the slot's items, from 0. |

Example input:


## slot.remove

Remove an item from a component instance's list with everything it holds, its translations and the motion wholly inside it, with the waits on that motion (a gate that opens when one of its timelines ends). `motion: false` leaves that motion, `waits: false` the waits. Refused: `slot.at_least` (the slot would hold fewer than its least items), `motion.starts_from_wait` (a timeline that stays starts from a wait it would take), `slot.no_item`, `slot.not_a_list`, `slot.unknown`. Output: { took: { timelines, states, locks } } of the motion it took, else null.

- **op**; class `sections` (Content author, Designer, Administrator); dry_run_ops judges it; one undo in History takes it back.
- Found by the plain words: "carousel", "slide", "card".

| Input | Type | Required | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | { page: uuid } \| { component: string } | yes | Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page. |
| `node` | string | yes | The component instance that holds the list (node/<pageId>?node= reads its slots). |
| `slot` | string | yes | The list's slot name, as the instance's definition declares it (definition/<key> lists its slots). |
| `item` | string | yes | The item to remove: one of the slot's items. |
| `motion` | false |  | false: the motion wholly inside the item stays where it is; absent: it goes with the item. |
| `waits` | false |  | false: the waits on its motion stay (a gate that opens when one of its timelines ends). |

Example input:

```json
{"at":{"page":"87c82653-80cd-4b17-ae54-aca941cbf8a2"},"node":"38c3kvuc","slot":"default","item":"s5g9nni6"}
```
